title: Can all four symmetry sketches be drawn?
description: Four rough sketches are asked for, a triangle and a four sided shape each time, with set numbers of fold lines and turns. Each sketch is folded and then turned to see which lines and angles of symmetry it has. The video breaks the idea that cutting a shape into two equal halves is enough; the halves must match when folded.
teaching_notes: One idea: test every sketch with a fold and a turn, then match the result to the rule asked. Watch for students who call any line that cuts a shape into equal halves a line of symmetry.

source: Figure it Out Q3 (section 9.2, second block)
video_script.why: The child learns to choose a triangle or a four sided shape for a given pattern of fold lines and turns, by testing each choice with a fold and a turn.
video_script.substitution: Sketch each shape on paper, fold it along every line that might work, then turn it about its centre to see which turns fit.
video_script.anchor: four rough sketches drawn one after the other on the same page
video_script.payoff_line: All four sketches can be drawn

final_answer.value: triangle with three equal sides: 3 lines, 3 angles; triangle with two equal sides: 1 line, no rotational symmetry; leaning parallelogram: no line, angles 180 and 360; trapezium with equal slanting sides: 1 line, no rotational symmetry
final_answer.spoken: a triangle with three equal sides has three lines and three angles, a triangle with two equal sides has one line and no turn, a leaning parallelogram has no line but a half turn fits, and a four sided shape with equal slanting sides has one line and no turn

hold_back: all four sketches can be drawn
never_show: the diagonal of a leaning parallelogram drawn as a line of symmetry
a triangle with exactly two lines of symmetry
maths_rules: triangle with 3 equal sides: 3 fold lines, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side
360 / 3 = 120, so it fits after 120, 240 and 360 degrees: 3 angles of symmetry
triangle with only 2 equal sides: 1 fold line, from the top corner to the middle of the third side; only 360 degrees fits, so no rotational symmetry
leaning parallelogram (no right angle, adjacent sides unequal): no fold line, neither the middle lines nor the diagonals; a half turn of 180 degrees fits, so its angles are 180 and 360

trapezium with one pair of parallel sides and equal slanting sides: 1 fold line through the middles of the parallel sides; a half turn does not fit because the parallel sides differ in length, so only 360 degrees fits
each of the four rules is met by its sketch, so all four can be drawn
video_script.design: One idea: the fold test and the turn test decide each sketch. Four sketches in turn, the fold lines in teal and the turns in amber, all on one page.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four empty boxes in a row on a page, the first two marked triangle and the last two marked four sided shape; a fold arrow and a turn arrow appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.rules: a fold arrow and a turn arrow appear above the four boxes
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the four boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about sketching triangles and four sided shapes.
<bookmark mark='rules'/>Each sketch must have a set number of fold lines and a set kind of turn.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can every one of the four sketches be drawn?

beats.on_screen: the four boxes hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a paper shape folds along a dashed teal line and the halves cover each other; then it turns about a red dot and fits again; only the full turn is marked for a shape that fits nowhere else

marks.line: a shape folds along a dashed teal line and the halves cover each other
marks.angle: the shape turns about a red dot and fits its outline again
marks.full: the full turn glows alone on the circle of turns

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>A fold line where both halves cover each other is called a line of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='angle'/>A turn that makes a shape look the same is called an angle of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='full'/>The full turn always fits. If only the full turn fits, the shape has no rotational symmetry.

beats.on_screen: Given: four sketches, each with its own rule about fold lines and turns

marks.given: the four rules are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, we need four sketches, each with its own rule about fold lines and turns.

beats.on_screen: To find: a triangle or a four sided shape for each rule

marks.find: the words a shape for each rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find a triangle or a four sided shape for each rule.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, first sketch: a triangle with 3 equal sides; 3 fold lines from each corner to the middle of the opposite side; 360 / 3 = 120; turns 120, 240, 360 degrees

marks.first: a triangle with three equal sides is drawn in the first box
marks.fold: three teal fold lines run from the corners to the middles of the opposite sides
marks.turn: the turns 120, 240 and 360 degrees are listed in amber

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, the first sketch. Take a triangle with three equal sides.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>Three folds work, from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>The turns of one hundred twenty, two hundred forty and three hundred sixty degrees all fit.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, second sketch: a triangle with only 2 equal sides; 1 fold line from the top corner to the middle of the third side; only the full turn fits

marks.second: a triangle with only two equal sides is drawn in the second box
marks.fold: one teal fold line runs from the top corner to the middle of the third side
marks.turn: the turn test is tried and only the full turn fits

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, the second sketch. Take a triangle with only two equal sides.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>Fold from the top corner to the middle of the third side, and the halves match.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>No other fold works, because the third side differs. No turn smaller than a full turn fits.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, third sketch: a leaning parallelogram with no right angle and unequal neighbouring sides; the folds along the middles and along a diagonal fail; a half turn fits; angles 180 and 360

marks.third: a leaning parallelogram is drawn in the third box
marks.fold: the folds along the middles and along a diagonal are tried and the halves do not match
marks.turn: the half turn fits and the angles 180 and 360 degrees are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step three, the third sketch. Take a parallelogram that leans, with no right angle and unequal neighbouring sides.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>Fold it along the middle or along a diagonal, and the halves do not match.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>It has no line of symmetry. A half turn about its centre fits. Its angles are one hundred eighty and three hundred sixty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, fourth sketch: a four sided shape with one pair of parallel sides and equal slanting sides; 1 fold line through the middles of the parallel sides; the half turn does not fit

marks.fourth: a four sided shape with one pair of parallel sides and equal slanting sides is drawn in the fourth box
marks.fold: one teal fold line joins the middles of the two parallel sides
marks.turn: the half turn is tried and the parallel sides do not land on each other

narration: <bookmark mark='fourth'/>Step four, the fourth sketch. Take a four sided shape with one pair of parallel sides and equal slanting sides.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>Fold along the line joining the middles of the two parallel sides, and the halves match.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>A half turn does not fit, because the parallel sides have different lengths.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, check: each sketch is put back against its rule; four ticks

marks.check: each sketch slides back to its rule and a tick appears
marks.four: the fourth tick appears and all four sketches glow

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, put the sketches back in the questions. The first has more than one line and more than one angle.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The second has one line and no turn. The third has a turn and no line. The fourth has one line and no turn.

beats.on_screen: Answer: triangle with three equal sides: 3 lines, 3 angles; triangle with two equal sides: 1 line, none; leaning parallelogram: no line, 180 and 360; four sided shape with equal slanting sides: 1 line, none

marks.ans: the four results are boxed one under the other
marks.quad: the two four sided results glow

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>All four sketches can be drawn.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>The triangle with three equal sides has three lines and three angles. The triangle with two equal sides has one line and no turn.
<bookmark mark='quad'/>The leaning parallelogram has a half turn but no line. The four sided shape with equal slanting sides has one line and no turn.
